comparator.name: Global Communication Science
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 public curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant
comparator.sourceNotes: UvA distinguishes the English Global Communication Science track from Dutch Communicatiewetenschap. The English study-programme table supplies 60 EC in each year. Year 1 contains seven compulsory courses (12+12+6+6+8+8+8 EC). Year 2 contains five 6-EC theory/research/practice courses, a 24-EC internationally oriented internship and a 6-EC internship case. Year 3 combines 30 EC of genuine open elective/minor/exchange space, one 6-EC communication-topic restricted elective, an 18-EC independent research project and 6 EC From Research to Impact. The named topic examples are not assigned as compulsory content; the 6-EC restricted choice is retained generically.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the English Global Communication Science track; UvA explicitly contrasts its international and cross-cultural focus with the Dutch Communicatiewetenschap track. This exact route is chosen independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Global media, communication and research
alternatives.concept: Studies media forms, their cultural and societal effects, cross-border public issues, persuasion, and empirical methods. A media and communication sequence combines quantitative and qualitative inquiry with climate communication, documentary and organisational contexts; UCR has no mandatory placement or communication-science research project equivalent.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed course list has six communication courses, six media courses, four direct methods courses and specific global/persuasion contexts.
progression: Media, communication and method introductions precede advanced persuasion, documentary and organisational study where feasible; six semesters, formal prerequisites, availability and six 300-level courses were verified against the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: International communication and audience strategy
alternatives.concept: Applies communication and media analysis to international organisations, consumer engagement, market research and intercultural audience strategy. It retains the empirical research and communication core but replaces crisis and environmental media topics with business, diversity and marketing practice.
alternatives.labelReason: Marketing, market research, international business, organisational psychology, diversity and audience validation make the applied strategy emphasis visible in the completed schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: The audience-strategy route adds Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Consumer Product Design, Market Research, International Business & Governance and Leadership & Diversity Management, while the broad route instead studies cross-border political crises, media archaeology, environmental media, sociology and youth extremism. More than four courses differ in each direction, changing the programme from global-public media analysis to communication decisions in international organisations.
progression: Foundational business and research courses precede marketing, market research, diversity and international business; six semesters, formal prerequisites, availability and seven 300-level courses were verified against the current enriched workbook.

selection.assessment: The broad route covers media effects, cross-cultural differences, global issues and research. The official marketing and organisation theme plus direct target-specific interests support a distinct applied strategy route. A third health-and-sustainability communication route has only a small number of direct UCR communication courses; filling 24 places would convert it into health or sustainability study rather than retain communication science as the organising field. Stop at two.

notes.text: UvA provides a continuous empirical communication-science sequence, compulsory 24-EC international internship and 18-EC research project. UCR combines media and rhetoric with research methods, psychology and applied settings, but does not reproduce a compulsory communication placement, content-analysis/statistical sequence or independent communication-science project. Its optional independent research element is a separate opportunity outside the scheduled 180 EC.
